day_shape: 71 items: IRGC navy reports oil tanker struck mine in Strait of Hormuz, Trump/Netanyahu issue fresh Iran strike threats, Germany summons Iranian ambassador over alleged Jewish community plot, Iran parliament confirms Akhlaki as defence minister (237 votes), Lavrov due in Tehran.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incident
threads.summary: Iran's IRGC navy said an oil tanker struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials outlined conditions for reopening the strait, and Qatar Airways extended cancellation of Riyadh and Dammam flights until 24 October.

threads.label: Trump-Netanyahu Iran strike threats
threads.summary: Trump said the US may "soon finish the job" against Iran while Netanyahu said Israel was prepared to strike without US support and vowed to topple Tehran's government. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Macron "made his bed" by siding with Washington, and Trump endorsed Netanyahu nine days before Israel's 27 October election.

threads.label: Iran diplomatic and cabinet moves
threads.summary: Germany's foreign ministry summoned the Iranian ambassador over an alleged attempted attack on German Jewish community leaders, and Russia's Lavrov is due in Tehran on Monday. Iran's parliament confirmed Mehrdad Akhlaki as Defence Minister with 237 votes in favour out of 277 cast.

threads.label: Yemen, Houthis and Gulf security
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported at least 18 killed in a Houthi attack on a Yemeni government military camp in Shabwa, as the UAE president and Saudi defence minister discussed regional security. Macron began a four-country Gulf tour covering Kuwait, UAE, Bahrain and Qatar through 21 October.

threads.label: Gaza operations and humanitarian cuts
threads.summary: The IDF announced a Hamas cell commander and two operatives were killed in weekend Gaza strikes, and released a document it said showed Hamas plans to plant explosives around displaced-persons camps. The World Food Programme said funding shortages will cut monthly food support for around 500,000 Gazans.

threads.label: Iran domestic economic strain
threads.summary: Iran International reported retiree protests across several Iranian cities over pensions, living costs and healthcare, and separate accounts of soaring hospital costs and staff shortages. OCHA's September humanitarian update said strikes in four southern provinces reportedly killed 18 and injured 142, with household purchasing power deteriorating further.

threads.label: Regime messaging: arrests, sport, unity
threads.summary: Iran's Ministry of Intelligence announced the arrest of 39 people in Qazvin described as "mercenaries of the American-Zionist enemy," while Khamenei's office issued congratulations to the under-23 freestyle wrestling team that took the world title in the United States. Defa Press and IRIB ran messaging on national cohesion, sacred-defence history and judiciary tolerance.

events.title_en: Hani-Zada: The European Union is in a state of collapse

events.summary_en: Macron begins his regional tour amid France protests Emmanuel Macron, President of France, arrived in Kuwait on Monday to begin his regional tour to four countries: Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar. This tour will continue until 21 October. This tour is taking place as regional tensions have increased and disruption to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's important oil transit passages, has raised concerns about energy supply. These developments coincide with widespread protests in France.

events.title: ‼️🔎REVEALED: An internal document belonging to Hamas detailing plans to plant explosive devices in areas of displaced persons camps in Gaza. The document shows that Hamas' engineering department proposed planting explosive devices around displaced persons camps and detonating them as IDF troops approached, placing the civilian population in the camps at risk, in order to create panic as a smokescreen for the escape of its operatives. This was part of Hamas’ preparations to protect its leadership and operatives, while endangering and exploiting the civilian population in the area, fully aware that these actions were likely to cause direct harm to civilians.
